producer_report.summary: Added `check_request_coverage` (new module reading/coverage.rs), wired as the last `step!` in `refusing_check`. At reading acceptance it parses the request's `Acceptance` bullets and refuses a reading whose criteria leave one out. The error names every omitted bullet verbatim and says to cover it or ask the split as a question. A bullet with paths, `--flags` or file names needs all of them in the criteria. Any other bullet needs one word that tells it from the other bullets and the request's other text to share a stem with a criterion word. Not checked: a reading that asks a question or declines; a request with no `Acceptance` heading; a request whose own non-bullet text affirmatively allows splitting the job (negated or conditional wording such as 'Do not split this job' does not count, and neither does this job's own request). The doc comment names the 2026-10-29 rejection and the question-only rule, and states that it refuses more readings, the higher refusal rate is intended, and the expected 10% is an estimate. Added 16 unit tests in reading.rs, 15 corpus cases with 13 new form tags, and a CHANGELOG item. To keep the suite green I made two fixture-level changes outside the listed files: the fake reader's criterion now repeats the request's bullets, and the drain-test helper `queue_steward_request` adds the bullet 'the tests still pass'. fmt, clippy -D warnings, the full test suite, the policy test and the mirrors test all pass.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: the plan left crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs unchanged and said to remove the Acceptance heading from a newly refused fixture. cargo test --locked showed 20 drain tests refused, caused by steward-rendered requests, whose Acceptance section the steward applier always writes, so the heading could not be dropped. I changed fake.rs (its one criterion now repeats the request's bullets, with a unit test) and the queue_steward_request helper in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (a text with no bullets gets the bullet 'the tests still pass'). The check itself is not weakened. Both files are outside the brief's listed deliverables.

The 10% newly refused share is an estimate. I could not run the producer-loop replay of stored accepted readings here, so the real share is unmeasured. If Athena's replay reports more than 15%, the plan's ordered loosening applies: (1) any one token instead of all tokens in is_covered, then (2) one more character of prefix tolerance in related().

A flaky failure was seen once in run::tests::produce_and_verify_order_tests::a_check_that_waited_checks_the_disk_again during a full run under load. It is disk related, passes alone and in the later full rerun, and does not touch reading code.
mistakes: My first expectation in coverage_stems_leave_out_stop_words_and_file_name_parts assumed 'unreleased' keeps its form, but the 'ed' strip gives 'unreleas'. I corrected the test before running it.

First fix attempt for the drain tests added two bullets, one of which ('README.md ends with a greeting line') was not stated by every scenario's reading. 12 tests still failed until I reduced it to the one bullet all scenarios share.
learnings: Shell hooks allow only cargo, chmod, git, ls, mv and rm. No cd, grep, tail, echo or paths outside the working copy, so logs have to go to a file inside it (and be removed after).

refusing_check is driven by step! lines, and the corpus test requires a refusing case for every one. The corpus base_reading copies the request's bullet lines as criteria, so every existing accepted corpus case with an Acceptance heading is covered by identical text.

queue_steward_request in drain.rs renders a steward request that always has an Acceptance section, and the drain tests use scripted readers with fixed criteria, so about 20 tests were newly refused until the helper added one bullet ('the tests still pass') that every scenario's reading states.

The deterministic fake reader had one stock criterion that covered no bullet. It now repeats the request's bullets in that one criterion, which keeps the criteria count at 1 for the fake producer and verifier.

A plain cargo test --locked stops at the first failing binary. A single disk-wait test (a_check_that_waited_checks_the_disk_again) failed once under load and passed on rerun, so --no-fail-fast is the way to see the rest.
desires: A way to run the producer-loop replay of accepted readings locally, to measure the real newly refused share instead of declaring an estimate.
Read-only access to a shell with grep, tail and cd, to inspect long test output without writing log files into the working copy.
